name: OmniRegex Engine
problem: Regular expression engines often rely on backtracking (NFA execution), making them susceptible to catastrophic catastrophic backtracking (ReDoS) and unpredictable latency spikes when processing complex patterns.
pain: Developers suffer from hidden exponential-time execution bugs when matching complex nested patterns with standard backtracking regex engines.
solution: Build a rigorous C11 regex compiler that translates AST patterns into an explicit Thompson NFA, converts it via subset construction to a deterministic DFA, minimizes states, and executes matching safely within explicit memory limits.
verification: Deterministic integration suite feeding malformed regex syntax, nested alternation loops, long adversarial strings, and invalid character class ranges to verify memory safety, correct matching boundaries, and immunity to catastrophic backtracking.
major_features: Custom lexer and recursive-descent parser building an explicit Regular Expression Abstract Syntax Tree
Thompson NFA construction engine mapping concatenation, alternation, and Kleene star operators
Powerset construction algorithm transforming non-deterministic finite automata into deterministic DFA transition tables
Hopcroft's DFA state minimization algorithm compressing redundant states to optimize memory footprint
Deterministic linear-time $O(n)$ matching execution engine operating without recursion or stack growth
Bytecode emission subsystem compiling minimized DFA tables into dense executable instruction streams
Captured group extraction engine tracking sub-expression match offsets via virtual register tracking
Exhaustive regression test suite verifying protection against catastrophic backtracking (ReDoS) vulnerabilities
truth_policy: Only validated behavior may be claimed as working.
